newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Vozrozhdeniye bank sold ADRs.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Vozrozhdeniye bank sold ADRs.

text.p: Foreign investors have bought three percent of the shares of Russian commercial bank AKB Vozrozhdeniye through an American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) programme, the bank said on Wednesday.
One ADR corresponds to one underlying share with a nominal value of 10,000 roubles, it said in a statement.
Sergei Malinin, deputy head of the bank's securities department, told Reuters that the market price of shares was around the nominal value, but said he was unable to give an exact price for the ADRs.
ING Bank Eurasia is the custodian and The Bank of New York the depositary bank.
Russian banks need the permission of the central bank to sell shares abroad. The central bank limits ADR programmes to three percent of a bank's capital.
Vozrozhdeniye's authorised capital is 102 billion roubles, against assets at the start of this year of 8.4 trillion.

Inkombank has also launched an ADR progamme, and Bank Menatep is planning one. But Russian bank shares are highly illiquid and rarely traded in Russia, with the exception of shares in the state savings bank Sberbank.
